_readme: verified: 'live' = fetched 2026-08-24 and returned real current items;
'untested' = plausible but NOT confirmed, test before trusting.
tier 2 = reputable press (may be cited as fact)
tier 3 = GTA specialist / aggregator (label the source)
tier 4 = unverified rumour surface (never auto-post; corroboration required)
tier 5 = documented fabricators / structural spam (hard block)

feeds.name: Rockstar Games (YouTube)
feeds.note: Best trailer-drop trigger available: free, unauthenticated, no quota. Channel ID verified; two candidate IDs found in blogs both 404'd.

feeds.name: Google News - GTA 6 query
feeds.note: The workhorse: ~100 items, every outlet, source name per item. Links are news.google.com wrappers and MUST be redirect-resolved before dedup.

feeds.name: Newswire proxy via Google News
feeds.note: Live, but NOT instant-alert eligible. Tested 2026-08-25: of 100 entries, ~39 came from socialclub/support/signin/store subdomains and several more were bare static page titles ('Rockstar Games', 'Grand Theft Auto V', 'Social Club Account'). Because Google News hands us only a wrapper URL, a real Newswire article (/newswire/article/...) cannot be distinguished from a static page by path. Instant alerts therefore stay on rockstar_youtube, which is an actual upload feed. min_title_words=5 drops the bare page titles; the non-news subdomains are in blocked_domains.

feeds.name: RockstarINTEL
feeds.note: GTA-dedicated and fast, but heavily leak-focused: on 2026-08-24 all three top items were leak coverage. Returned 429 when its main and tag feeds were fetched back-to-back - needs a per-domain delay.

feeds.name: Rockstar Newswire
feeds.note: DISABLED. Cloudflare returns 403 based on the TLS ClientHello fingerprint before headers are read, so no User-Agent fixes it, and a Chrome UA makes it worse. Defeating it (curl_cffi) would circumvent a deliberate access control and Rockstar's ToS prohibits automated access. Use google_news_rockstar_site instead.

feeds.name: Take-Two investor relations
feeds.note: Verified live 2026-08-26; carries 'Rockstar Games Announces Pre-Orders for Grand Theft Auto VI'. THE gap this closes: pre-orders, price, platform lists, edition changes and delays are all announced as TEXT, which the YouTube feed cannot see - so the bot previously learned them second-hand from tier-2 press hours later and could never instant-alert them. Safe to mark instant: non-GTA releases self-filter on relevance (verified: 'NBA 2K27 Cover Athletes Revealed' is correctly rejected).

feeds.name: Cfx.re / FiveM announcements
feeds.note: Verified live 2026-08-26. The only feed whose items the audience can act on THIS WEEK rather than in 2027 - e.g. 'Support for GTA Online: The Kortz Center Heist Update is Available Now' and 'Public Stress Test Calendar: FiveM for GTAV Enhanced'. Rockstar has owned Cfx.re since Aug 2023, so this is first-party for the GTA 5 RP platform the community actually runs. Not instant: useful, rarely urgent.

feeds.name: Xbox Wire (Grand Theft Auto tag)
feeds.note: Platform-holder first-party. Tag-scoped, so 8 entries span 2021-2026 and it is effectively noise-free. Carried the Nov 19 2026 pre-order announcement and the trailer post independently of the Newswire, which is unreachable behind Cloudflare.

feeds.name: PlayStation Blog (GTA VI tag)
feeds.note: Platform-holder first-party. Carried 'GTA VI plays best on PS5 November 19'.

feeds.name: IGN
feeds.note: IGN was the single largest coverage hole: #1 domain in the database with no direct feed, so every item arrived as a Google News wrapper. This variant is chosen over the feedburner ones because feedburner is in canonical._REDIRECT_HOSTS and costs an extra round-trip per item.

feeds.name: GamesIndustry.biz
feeds.note: Trade press; carries the Take-Two legal and business coverage others miss.

_publisher_names_note: Display names by domain. Without this the raw feed title leaks into the digest as the attribution ('Eurogamer.net Latest Articles Feed', 'GameSpot - Game News'). Attribution is an editorial requirement here, so it should read like a masthead.

_domain_tier_notes.polygon.com: Deliberately tier 3, not 2: research found no GTA-specific track record either way and refused to rate on reputation alone. Promote if it earns it.
_domain_tier_notes.insider-gaming.com: Demoted from tier 2. Published then fully retracted the CyberLeek 'dead man's switch' story on 2026-08-22. Tom Henderson also has Rockstar-specific misses (RDR remaster that shipped as a port, a Bully revival that never came) - accurate on Battlefield/CoD, which is domain-transfer reputation inflation.
_domain_tier_notes.bbc.com: Tier 2 with a caveat: ran a GTA 6 '30-minute special' claim with no official source.
_domain_tier_notes.torrentfreak.com: Tier 2 for copyright/legal coverage ONLY - the best source on the 2026 leak wave's legal dimension.
_domain_tier_notes.bloomberg.com: Tier 2 for written articles only (Jason Schreier). Podcast/offhand remarks get hedge-stripped by aggregators.

_blocked_domain_notes: Two groups. (1) Rockstar's own non-news subdomains: socialclub/support/signin/store serve account pages and support articles, not news, but a site: query indexes them and they would otherwise be tiered 1 and posted as official announcements. (2) Parasite SEO: legitimate institutions' subdomains hosting spam. Near-100% precision rule - Stanford does not report on GTA 6 map leaks. Blocked on structural grounds, which is not an accusation of fabrication against the institution.
_blocked_handle_notes: Documented fabrication (zapactugta6 admitted AI fake gameplay, 8M views in 24h; GTASixJoker got a Take-Two C&D and apologised 2026-04-24; elefelelen built the March 2026 Vice City bridge fake and self-debunked), plus the CyberLeek impostor cluster and one satire account whose output is mistaken for news anyway.

factual_baseline._note: Used to flag items that contradict established fact. Update after each official announcement. Verified 2026-08-24.
factual_baseline.online_mode: not announced; Rockstar markets GTA VI as a single-player experience

corroboration._note: 'Independent' means: different parent company, no citation link between the two reports, and >20 minutes apart. Five outlets reporting one 4chan post is ONE source.
